note: Para 23(3). The on-screen fragment is verbatim.

claim: That warning line is on your statement too
source_quote: shall be prominently displayed in all the billing statements
note: Para 23(3) (commercial banks; RRBs have the same rule).

claim: India has about 11.86 crore credit cards; RBI data as of March 2026 (on-screen: 11.86 CRORE CARDS [RBI DATA | MAR 2026])
note: RBI Bank-wise ATM/POS/Card Statistics, March 2026 (Revised), Total row, credit cards outstanding: 118,633,677 = 11.86 crore. The VO says 'now': newer RBI data exist. August 2026: 124,053,544 (12.41 crore; RBI atmid=186; Business Standard 24 Sep 2026: 'rose to 124.05 million in August'). Recommended update in fact-check.md.

claim: Cardholders owe the banks about ₹2.98 lakh crore (on-screen: ₹2.98 LAKH CRORE OUTSTANDING [RBI BULLETIN | SEP 2026])
note: RBI Bulletin Sep 2026, Current Statistics, 'Deployment of Gross Bank Credit by Major Sectors', row 4.5, ₹ crore. The PDF is captcha-gated; the row was read through the search-engine index (NOT machine-checked). Reference date: 31 Jul 2026. RBI's July 2026 sectoral release (prid=63478) compares 'the fortnight ended July 31, 2026' with 'July 25, 2025', and 297,756 / 291,088 = +2.3% and 297,756 / 294,461 = +1.1% match the row's growth columns. Covers 41 select banks (~95% of non-food credit), so 'owe the banks' is right; NBFC issuers such as SBI Card are outside it. Recommended tag: … · JUL 2026 [RBI DATA].

claim: Reference date of the ₹2.98 lakh crore figure (fortnight ended 31 Jul 2026)
source_quote: On a year-on-year (y-o-y) basis, non-food bank credit2 grew by 19.1 per cent as on the fortnight ended July 31, 2026, compared to 9.9 per cent during the corresponding fortnight of the previous year (i.e., July 25, 2025).
note: Other figure for the description: TransUnion CIBIL puts outstanding card balances (all lenders) at ₹3.1 lakh crore as of March 2026 (Business Today, 8 Jul 2026).

claim: CRIF High Mark: ₹33,886 crore of card dues were 91–360 days overdue as of March 2025 (on-screen: ₹33,886 CR · 91–360 DAYS OVERDUE [CRIF HIGH MARK | MAR 2025])
source_quote: Credit card delinquencies in the 91–360 days overdue category rose 44.3 per cent year-on-year, from Rs 23,475.6 crore in March 2024 to Rs 33,886.5 crore in March 2025, according to a report by CRIF High Mark.
note: Business Standard 3 Aug 2025. Also Free Press Journal 28 Jul 2025 and Angel One 30 Jul 2025 (both from The Indian Express's report of CRIF data; indianexpress.com was not reachable). On-screen text is right.

claim: VO: 'Of this [the ₹2.98 lakh crore], the money unpaid for more than ninety days' = ₹33,886 crore
source_quote: According to data from CRIF High Mark, credit card payments that are overdue between 91 and 360 days have increased by 44% in one year.
note: Two problems: (1) the CRIF figure is the 91–360-day bucket, not everything past 90 days (the 360+ bucket is left out); (2) 'of this' links a March 2025 CRIF figure (all lenders) to a July 2026 RBI bank figure. FIX the VO (fact-check.md). Picture: show it as its own red stack dated MAR 2025, not as a slice of the ₹2.98 lakh crore tower.

claim: That overdue amount rose 44% in one year (on-screen: +44% IN ONE YEAR [CRIF HIGH MARK | MAR 2025])
source_quote: According to CRIF High Mark data, unpaid dues between 91 and 360 days shot up 44% year-on-year to ₹33,886 crore by March 2025.
note: Business Standard gives 44.3% (₹23,475.6 crore → ₹33,886.5 crore).

claim: Per a central statistics ministry survey, the share of adults in debt is highest in Andhra Pradesh (43.7%) and Telangana (37.2%) (on-screen: AP 43.7% · TELANGANA 37.2% OF ADULTS IN DEBT)
source_quote: Data showed that more than two out of five people in Andhra Pradesh are indebted (43.7 per cent), followed by Telangana (37.2 per cent), Kerala (29.9 per cent), Tamil Nadu (29.4 per cent), Puducherry (28.3 per cent), and Karnataka (23.2 per cent).
note: AP first, Telangana second among states/UTs, so 'highest in the country in AP and Telangana' holds. 'Adults' = people aged 15 and over: 'Indebtedness was measured for individuals aged 15 and above (adults)'. Indebted = an outstanding cash loan of ₹500 or more. National ≈15% (ThePrint: 14.7%).

claim: Source label: MoSPI survey, 2020–21 (on-screen tag [MoSPI SURVEY | 2020–21])
source_quote: The study used unit-level data from the National Statistics Office (NSO) 78th round (2020–21) Multiple Indicator Survey (MIS).
note: The percentages come from a study in MoSPI's journal Sarvekshana (Business Standard, 24 Oct 2025) built on the NSO's 2020–21 Multiple Indicator Survey. Recommended tag: [NSO SURVEY 2020–21 · MoSPI SARVEKSHANA]; optional 'PEOPLE 15+' instead of 'ADULTS'.

claim: Among complaints to the RBI Ombudsman, credit cards are in second place (on-screen: CARDS: #2 … FY 2024–25 [RBI OMBUDSMAN REPORT | DEC 2025])
source_quote: Complaints related to credit cards increased by 20.04 per cent and became the second-highest contributor.
note: Business Standard 1 Dec 2025; loans and advances first at 29.25%. Report coverage dated 1–2 Dec 2025, so the tag 'DEC 2025' is right.

claim: About 50,800 credit card complaints in one year (on-screen: ~50,811 COMPLAINTS · FY 2024–25)
source_quote: credit card complaints saw a significant surge of 20% to 50,811, accounting for 17.15% of the total complaints.
note: Outlook Money 2 Dec 2025: 'receiving a total of 50,811 complaints during the year'. 50,811 / 2,96,321 complaints at the Ombudsman offices = 17.15%.

claim: There was a sixteen-year court fight over these rates (on-screen: 2008 → 2024)
source_quote: Judgment & Order dated 07.07.2008 passed by the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Delhi
note: Civil Appeal No. 5273 of 2008, decided 20 Dec 2024 = 16 years in the Supreme Court. The complaint itself was filed in 2007 (Consumer Complaint no. 51 of 2007), so the whole case ran about 17 years; '16 years' fits the 2008 → 2024 framing on screen.

claim: In 2008 the National Consumer Commission ruled that charging more than 30% interest on credit cards was unfair (on-screen: NCDRC, 2008: ABOVE 30% = UNFAIR [BAR & BENCH | DEC 2024])
source_quote: (i) Charging of interest rates in excess of 30% p.a. from the credit card holders by banks for the former’s failure to make full payment on the due date or paying the minimum amount due, is an unfair trade practice.
note: NCDRC order of 07.07.2008 as quoted in the Supreme Court judgment. Note: the NCDRC finding was tied to failing to pay in full or paying only the minimum, which is this film's exact subject. Bar & Bench (20 Dec 2024) reports the same.

claim: In December 2024 the Supreme Court set that ruling aside (on-screen: SUPREME COURT, 20 DEC 2024: CAP SET ASIDE)
source_quote: The Supreme Court on Friday set aside the judgment of the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (NCDRC) from 2008 which held that banks charging interest in excess of 30 percent on credit card dues would amount to unfair trade practice
note: Judgment signed 'NEW DELHI DECEMBER 20, 2024' (Bela M. Trivedi and Satish Chandra Sharma JJ.); 20 Dec 2024 was a Friday.

claim: The court said interest rates are a matter within the RBI's domain
source_quote: A policy decision pertaining to the rate of interest, and trade practices carried out by the banks across the country, is a regulatory function within the specific statutory domain of the Reserve Bank of India and cannot come under the purview of judicial scrutiny by the National Commission.
note: Para 46. Para 51 calls the 30% cap 'an encroachment upon the domain of the Reserve Bank of India'.

claim: The court said customers are told the rate upfront
source_quote: once the terms of the credit card operations were known to the complainants and disclosed by the banking institutions before the issuance of the credit cards, the National Commission could not have scrutinized the terms or conditions, including the rate of interest.
note: Para 63; para 69: customers 'are made aware of ‘the most important terms and conditions’, including the rate of interest'. The VO paraphrases (marked as a paraphrase).

claim: Citation HSBC v. Awaz, 2024 INSC 1044 (on-screen tag)
note: Full title: Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corp. Ltd. v. Awaz & Ors., Civil Appeal No. 5273 of 2008 (with four connected appeals).

claim: Today there is no court-set limit on credit card interest; your rate is written in your card's MITC (on-screen: NO COURT CAP · CHECK YOUR MITC)
source_quote: there is no question of the RBI being directed to impose any cap on the rate of interest, either on the banking sector as a whole, or in respect of any one particular bank
note: Para 71. RBI also sets no cap: banks must set a Board-approved ceiling (Directions 2025 para 22). ICICI: the rate 'is always mentioned in the card’s Fees & Charges document and the Most Important Terms & Conditions (MITC)'.

claim: 'Card rotation': some people borrow for a day to pay the bill, then pull the money back out with the same card through an app 'in the name of rent' (on-screen: BORROW → PAY → PULL OUT → RETURN · ILLUSTRATION)
source_quote: The rule aims to ensure stronger diligence and prevent misuse of credit cards for peer-to-peer transfers disguised as merchant payments.
note: Business Standard 18 Sep 2025 (users also used rent payments to 'manage cash flow'). The described sequence is an illustration (labelled).

claim: Rotation does not reduce the debt; it only moves the due date a month and adds a fee each time (on-screen: DEBT: SAME · DUE DATE: +1 MONTH · + FEES)
source_quote: For fintechs, the change means losing a high-volume use case that boosted card spends and convenience fee income.
note: Fees on card rent payments: Mint via GoCredit (10 Jun 2026) cites platform fees of 1.5–2%.

claim: In September 2025 the RBI brought new rules for payment aggregators (on-screen: RBI PA DIRECTIONS · 15 SEP 2025)
source_quote: A PA shall aggregate funds only for the merchant with whom it has a contractual relationship.
note: Reserve Bank of India (Regulation of Payment Aggregators) Directions, 2025, RBI/DPSS/2025-26/141, dated September 15, 2025 (rbi.org.in).

claim: After that, apps like PhonePe, Paytm and CRED removed the option to pay rent by credit card (tag [BUSINESS STANDARD · MEDIANAMA | SEP 2025])
source_quote: Fintech giants PhonePe, Paytm and Cred have discontinued rent payment services after the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) changed the way Payment Aggregators (PAs) operate.
note: MediaNama 18 Sep 2025 agrees. UPDATE: in June 2026 PhonePe and CRED began piloting card rent payments again under a marketplace model with PAN cards of payer and payee and the rent agreement (Free Press Journal 9 Jun 2026; Storyboard18 9 Jun 2026, both citing Moneycontrol). A full public relaunch was not confirmed as of 11 Oct 2026. Recommended addition in fact-check.md.

claim: Cash drawn on a credit card carries a fee and interest from the day of withdrawal (on-screen: CASH: FEE + INTEREST FROM DAY 1 [ICICI BANK · INTEREST RATES PAGE | 2025])
source_quote: Unlike purchases, cash advances typically attract interest from the date of withdrawal, along with a cash advance fee.
note: HDFC MITC: 'Finance charges on cash advances are applicable from the date of transaction until the payment is made in full.' 'Even more dangerous' is the narrator's judgement.

claim: Auto-debit can be set for the total amount rather than the minimum (on-screen: AUTO-PAY THE TOTAL, NOT THE MINIMUM)
source_quote: How can I change the Auto Debit option from Minimum Amount Due to Total Amount Due or vice versa?
note: ICICI FAQ; HDFC MITC describes standing instructions with a TAD/MAD amount.

claim: Pay in full and the card is truly free: up to forty days of interest-free credit
source_quote: The interest free credit period could range from 20 to 50 days subject to the scheme applicable on the specific Credit Card
note: 40 days is only our example's longest band. General maximums: HDFC 20–50 days (MITC, 8 Oct 2026); ICICI 'typically ranges between 18-48 days' (FAQ). FIX: 'depending on the card, up to fifty days' (fact-check.md).

claim: Interest on money you pay stops that day, so the more you pay the less interest on what's left (on-screen: MORE PAID = LESS INTEREST [ICICI BANK · INTEREST RATES PAGE | 2025])
source_quote: On the Residual Amount (from Transaction Date to the Payment Received Date, whenever received in full)
note: ICICI's method charges the paid part only to the payment date and the residual after it.

claim: Paying at least the minimum means no late fee and no damage to your CIBIL report
source_quote: “Paying MAD will ensure that your credit score is not impacted. You will also avoid paying a late fee. However, the interest on the due amount will keep accumulating,” says Radhika Binani, chief product officer, Paisabazaar.
note: Business Standard 3 Aug 2025; RBI 23(5)/5(17); HDFC MITC on late fees. True for the payment record; high utilisation can still lower the score (M019). Optional precision in fact-check.md.

claim: First month: a partial payment can't avoid the backdated interest; paying ₹29,999 (₹1 short) still costs about ₹1,484 interest + GST (on-screen: PAID ₹29,999 (₹1 SHORT) → ₹1,484 INTEREST+GST [OUR CALCULATION · ICICI METHOD, 45% P.A.])
source_quote: Interest free period is cancelled in the event customer does not pay the Total Amount Due (TAD) by the Payment Due Date (PDD)
note: ₹1,483.91 in the tool and also with ICICI's day count (the extra purchase day and the shorter pre-payment segment cancel when ₹1 is left). Label present. English nit: 'however much you pay' means 'however much short of the full amount'.

claim: Once you clear the whole balance, the interest-free period comes back (on-screen: CLEAR IT ALL → FREE PERIOD RETURNS [HDFC BANK MITC])
source_quote: This period will be free of interest only if all previous dues are paid in full and there is no unpaid balance carried over from previous months.
note: HDFC MITC 8 Oct 2026; finance charges on new spends apply only 'till such time as the previous outstanding amounts are repaid in full'. ICICI FAQ: no interest 'provided the previous balance is cleared in full'.

claim: While a balance remains, every new swipe on that card is charged interest from that day
source_quote: On all new transactions (from the transaction date) till such time as the previous outstanding amounts are paid in full
note: Same rule as M048.

claim: Banks can convert a large card balance into EMIs; ask the bank (on-screen: 4 · ASK FOR AN EMI CONVERSION)
source_quote: When you convert your Credit Card outstanding balance to EMI through SmartEMI
note: HDFC SmartEMI page (fetched 11 Oct 2026).

claim: HDFC's EMI page showed rates of roughly 12–25%, far below 45% (on-screen: ≈12–25% vs 45% … [HDFC BANK SMARTEMI PAGE | APR–JUN 2025])
source_quote: Rate offered to the customer during the period of 1st April 2026 to June 30th 2026
note: Out of date. The live page now shows Q1 2026-27 (Apr–Jun 2026): Min IRR 10.80%, Max IRR 24.96%, Avg 18.20%, APR 21.57%. The 11.88–24.84% range was an older quarter. FIX: 'roughly eleven to twenty-five percent'; tag APR–JUN 2026 (recheck the page before publishing in case it moves to Q2).

claim: EMI conversion carries a processing fee plus GST: add both before saying yes
source_quote: a processing fee up to ₹ 999 (Exclusive of GST for all loan amounts) is applied
note: Fee is now up to ₹999 + GST (the writer's notes had ₹849). The film quotes no amount, so no change is needed.

claim: Stay away from unknown loan apps; they are an even bigger trap
source_quote: These reports also refer to excessive rates of interest and additional hidden charges being demanded from borrowers; adoption of unacceptable and high-handed recovery methods
note: RBI press release 23 Dec 2020, 'RBI Cautions against unauthorised Digital Lending Platforms/Mobile Apps'. Advice line.

claim: Under RBI rules banks must let you change the billing cycle at least once
source_quote: cardholders shall be provided option to modify the billing cycle of the credit card at least once, as per cardholders’ convenience.
note: Para 29 of the 2025 Directions (still in force; same text in RBI's RRB Directions).

claim: On-screen tag for the billing-cycle rule: [RBI CARD DIRECTIONS 2025 · PARA 23]
source_quote: cardholders shall be provided option to modify the billing cycle of the credit card at least once, as per cardholders’ convenience.
note: It is para 29. FIX on-screen: 5 · MOVE THE DUE DATE AFTER PAYDAY [RBI CARD DIRECTIONS 2025 · PARA 29].

claim: Your card's Key Fact Statement and MITC list the interest rate and charges
source_quote: Card-issuers shall provide a one-page Key Fact Statement along with the credit card application containing the important aspects of the card such as rate of interest, quantum of charges, among others.
note: Para 11(1); MITC contents para 91 (fees, interest-free period, finance charges). HDFC's document is titled 'KEY FACT STATEMENT CUM MOST IMPORTANT TERMS & CONDITIONS'.

claim: A non-zero 'finance charges' or 'interest' line on the statement means you are paying interest
source_quote: Finance Charge applies only if the outstanding balance on your card is not paid in full by the Payment Due Date.
note: ICICI statements call the line 'Interest Charges'.

claim: Complain to the bank first; if there's no proper reply within 30 days you can complain on RBI's CMS portal (on-screen: BANK FIRST → 30 DAYS → cms.rbi.org.in [RBI INTEGRATED OMBUDSMAN SCHEME])
source_quote: the complainant had not received any reply within 30 days after the Regulated Entity received the complaint
note: RB-IOS 2021 clause 10(2)(a), reproduced on Bank of Baroda's site; also a rejected or unsatisfactory reply qualifies, and the Ombudsman complaint must follow within a year. RBI Directions 2025 para 85 says the same and names https://cms.rbi.org.in.

claim: Recap: the minimum protects you from the late fee and from CIBIL damage, but not from interest (on-screen: MINIMUM ≠ NO INTEREST)
source_quote: It is the minimum sum you must pay by the due date to avoid late payment fees. Interest will continue to apply on the remaining balance.
note: CIBIL part as in M018/M085 (payment record; utilisation caveat in M019).

claim: Three numbers: 45% interest, 18% GST on it, and zero free days on new spends while a balance remains (on-screen: 45% · 18% GST · 0 FREE DAYS)
source_quote: However, this is not applicable if the Previous month's balance has not been cleared in full or if the Cardmember has availed of cash from ATM.
note: 45% = ICICI and HDFC standard rate (rows M034); 18% GST (row M038). 45% is not universal (SBI Card up to 42%; HDFC premium cards 23.88%); optional wording in fact-check.md.

claim: Next video: the three-day rule after the due date and CIBIL reporting (on-screen: +3 DAYS)
source_quote: 4. The above amendments shall come into force from April 01, 2027.
note: The three-day rule is in force now (2025 Directions para 23(5), effective 28 Nov 2025; it dates back to the 2022 Master Direction). The 2026 Amendment (RBI/2026-27/29, 27 Apr 2026) re-issues 23(5) from 1 Apr 2027 with the same wording; only the cross-reference changes to the 2026 Asset Classification Directions. TaxGuru's summary wrongly calls it a new rule.
